snip.t: Verapamil/Diltiazem: Contraindicated in wide-complex tachycardia of unknown origin (can trigger ventricular fibrillation) and decompensated heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.

qs.q: A child experiences sudden cardiac arrest due to ventricular fibrillation associated with long QT syndrome. What is the primary initial treatment required to re-establish an effective ventricular beat?
o: Administration of oral calcium channel blockers
qs.e: Ventricular fibrillation requires immediate DC defibrillation and CPR, followed by IV amiodarone or lidocaine if ineffective. Synchronized cardioversion is used for organized tachycardias rather than chaotic VF.

qs.q: A patient is brought in with an acute myocardial infarction and experiences ventricular fibrillation within the first few days. According to the clinical notes, what does this represent?
o: A rare late complication occurring several months after injury
An adverse drug effect resulting from intravenous heparin use
The most common cause of early post-infarction mortality
A structural mechanical complication linked to pseudoaneurysms
qs.e: Ventricular arrhythmia, including ventricular fibrillation or ventricular tachycardia, is the most common cause of death in the first few days after an MI. It requires immediate use of a defibrillator and CPR.
